evidence: The Fear and Greed Index sits at 11 ('Extreme Fear'), with a 7-day average of 9.71 and a 30-day average of 24.8. Sentiment has hovered in deep extreme fear for nearly three weeks, hitting a trough of 6 on February 7 before modestly stabilizing between 9 and 14 over the past four days. While prolonged extreme fear highlights persistent downward market pressure, sustained single-digit and low-double-digit readings historically act as a contrarian indicator of potential seller exhaustion and short-term relief bounces over a 24-hour horizon. This produces a slight directional lean toward an upward move.
limitations: Fear & Greed Index is a composite sentiment metric and does not incorporate real-time order book liquidity or intra-day market flows.
Sustained extreme fear can persist during extended macro downtrends without triggering immediate mean-reversion rallies.
Snapshot availability and later revisions are caller-attested, not independently verified.
